Changes film exposure and its imaging response, not simply the brightness of the final photo.
Adjusts the brightness of the final photo.
Adjusts print contrast. The default preserves the original effect. Bypassed in direct scan mode.
Fine-tunes warmth through print filtration, not a color temperature setting in K. Bypassed in direct scan mode.

Changes color and edge contrast through development inhibition. Controls the same effect as Development inhibition strength in Development; the two underlying factors are multiplied. The scale indicates a relative adjustment, with the default preserving the original effect. The minimum does not produce black and white.
Simulates a lens diffusion filter, controlled separately from film halation. Glimmerglass / Black Pro-Mist / Pro-Mist / Cinebloom correspond to their respective filter models.
Select a diffusion filter first. 0 disables the effect.
Controls the spread of lens diffusion.
Simulates film halation around highlights, usually warm-toned, with separately adjustable color. It does not blur the entire photo.
Controls the spread of film halation around highlights.
0 disables grain. Higher values increase film grain.
Controls grain size. Unavailable when strength is 0.
Selects a photographic paper or motion-picture print film profile, changing print color and response.
Changes yellow filtration during paper exposure. 0 uses the original formula. This is not screen color temperature.
Changes magenta filtration during paper exposure. 0 uses the original formula.

Adds a small, uniform exposure (also called preflashing) to paper or motion-picture print film to alter contrast. 0 disables it. The value is an additional exposure ratio, not flash power or image brightness.
Emphasizes scanned edges. 0 disables sharpening. Excessive strength may create halos; it cannot recover detail missing from the original.
Controls the sharpening radius in pixels. Unavailable when strength is 0.
Selects a bundled film profile. Reversal film defaults to direct scanning; negative film defaults to printing.
The simulated format\'s long-edge length in millimeters, not the film strip width. Affects grain and optical effect scale. 35 mm does not mean the long edge of a standard 135 frame.

Select a metering mode to enable auto exposure. Turning it off retains the last metering mode. Estimates film exposure from the imported photo, not the camera exposure at capture. Average and Median use brightness across the whole image; Center-weighted emphasizes the center; Partial meters only the central circle; Matrix weights a 5×5 grid; Multi-zone weights three concentric regions; Highlight-weighted emphasizes brighter pixels. These are simulated metering modes, not recreations of camera manufacturers\' scene recognition.
Increases exposure in highlight areas. 0 disables it.
Controls the area affected by highlight boost.
Sets the brightness at which highlight boost starts, in stops above middle gray. Higher values boost only brighter areas. This does not recover lost highlights.
Simulates lens blur, measured in micrometers at the film plane. 0 disables it.
Light scattering within the film, controlled independently of film halation.
Controls the spread of film scattering.
Changes the distribution of halation across color layers while preserving total strength.
Simulates the number of internal light reflections in the film. More reflections require more computation.
Controls halation decay after each reflection.
Compensates for the overall brightening caused by added halation. Turning this off retains that brightening.
Adjusts the grain area ratio for this color layer, not saturation or radius.
Simulates grain in the film\'s different light-sensitive layers.
Only applies when layered grain is off. More layers require more computation.
Adjusts grain blur in pixels of the image currently being processed. The default is 0.65.
The appearance of color film grain is related to tiny dye clouds. This adjusts dye cloud spread in the model. The value is a model coefficient, not a physical length.
Changes grain uniformity while preserving the profile\'s color-layer ratios.
Simulates the scale of uneven grain distribution, in micrometers. It does not represent actual grains sticking together.
Adjusts the strength of uneven grain distribution, with model amplitude in nanometers. This is neither actual grain displacement nor a percentage.
Adjusts the slope of the film characteristic curve. 1 uses the original profile value.

Simulates developer inhibitor effects within a layer and between color layers. Controls the same effect as Development inhibition in Adjustments; the two underlying factors are multiplied. The scale indicates a relative adjustment, with the default preserving the original effect.
Developer inhibitor diffusion distance in the model, in micrometers.
Adjusts development interactions within the same light-sensitive layer.
Adjusts development interactions between different light-sensitive layers.

Printing uses the selected photographic paper or motion-picture print film model. Direct scanning of reversal film produces a positive image. Direct scanning of negative film does not invert it and preserves the negative appearance.
Uses a diffusion filter at the printing stage. Does not apply to direct scans.
Adjusts the strength of print diffusion.
Adjusts the spread of print diffusion.
Uses neutralizing filtration from the film and paper database. Turn this off to adjust cyan, magenta and yellow filtration manually.
Manual neutralizing filtration. Determined by the database when auto neutralization is on.
Adjusts the characteristic curve slope of the selected paper or motion-picture print film model. 1 uses the original profile value.
Adjusts the characteristic curve slope of the high-speed sublayer in the print model. 1 uses the original profile value.
Adjusts the characteristic curve slopes of both the medium-speed and low-speed sublayers in the print model. 1 uses the original profile value.
Adjusts the characteristic curve slope of the red channel in the print model. 1 uses the original profile value.
Adjusts the characteristic curve slope of the green channel in the print model. 1 uses the original profile value.
Adjusts the characteristic curve slope of the blue channel in the print model. 1 uses the original profile value.
Simulates how developer depletion affects the characteristic curve of paper or motion-picture print film. 0 disables it. This does not simulate local chemical concentration.
Selects the light source used for printing. Direct scan mode bypasses printing.
Compensates during printing for brightness changes caused by film exposure adjustments. The effect also depends on print exposure normalization.
Normalizes print exposure using middle gray as a reference. This is not automatic metering based on analysis of the whole photo.
Sets separate yellow filtration for print pre-exposure. Has no effect when pre-exposure is off.
Sets separate magenta filtration for print pre-exposure. Has no effect when pre-exposure is off.
Simulates slight scan blur, in pixels of the image currently being processed. 0 disables it.
Simulates haze and reduced contrast caused by stray light, not film halation around highlight edges. 0 disables it.
Controls local variation in scan glare.
Smooths uneven scan glare, in pixels of the image currently being processed.
Corrects the scan white point. Not supported for direct scans of negatives; select printing or reversal film.
Corrects the scan black point. Not supported for direct scans of negatives; select printing or reversal film.
Target for white-point correction. Must be higher than the black point.
Target for black-point correction. Must be lower than the white point.
Compresses colors outside the sRGB gamut into the displayable range. Automatically disabled for wide-gamut export.

Experimental resident or banded GPU rendering. Some effects use approximations and may differ from CPU output. Falls back to CPU when budgets or device support are insufficient. Speed gains are not guaranteed.
White sprocket holes on negatives; always white on reversal film

The film model is based on Andrea Volpato\'s spektrafilm and its Rust port. The interface and image processing integration have been modified. Software is provided under GPL-3.0; film data under CC BY-SA 4.0. RAW decoding uses rawler (LGPL-2.1). Each dependency retains its own license. Complete corresponding source and build materials are provided with the installation package. Legal texts are kept in their original language.
